question: Secondary thyroid disease is not suspected in an adult. Which initial test does NG145 say to consider?
explanation: NG145 says consider measuring TSH alone for adults when secondary thyroid dysfunction is not suspected [1].
sourceArticle: Thyroid disease: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG145)

question: TSH is below the reference range on that initial test. What should be measured in the same sample?
explanation: If TSH is below the reference range, measure FT4 and FT3 in the same sample. If TSH is above the range, measure FT4 in the same sample [1].
sourceArticle: Thyroid disease: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG145)

question: TSH is above the reference range. Which free hormone does NG145 add?
explanation: If TSH is above the reference range, measure free thyroxine (FT4) in the same sample [1].
sourceArticle: Thyroid disease: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG145)

question: What is first-line treatment of primary hypothyroidism in NG145?
explanation: Offer levothyroxine as first-line treatment for adults, children, and young people with primary hypothyroidism [1].
sourceArticle: Thyroid disease: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG145)

question: Why does NG145 say not to offer liothyronine routinely?

options.A: It is first-line in pregnancy only
options.B: There is not enough evidence that it offers benefit over levothyroxine, alone or in combination
options.C: It is more effective than levothyroxine in every trial
options.D: It replaces the need for TSH monitoring
options.E: It is recommended for all subclinical disease

correctAnswerText: There is not enough evidence that it offers benefit over levothyroxine, alone or in combination
explanation: Do not routinely offer liothyronine for primary hypothyroidism, either alone or combined with levothyroxine, because there is not enough evidence that it offers additional benefit [1].
sourceArticle: Thyroid disease: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG145)
